questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that a lab evaluating its own model faces a structural problem, even assuming complete good faith?
options: Because labs lack the technical skill to evaluate their own models
Because commercial pressure to ship and closeness to the product both push toward reassuring interpretations, independent of any individual's intent
Because self-evaluation is illegal in every jurisdiction
Because labs never run any internal safety testing at all
questions.explain: The conflict is structural — built into being both the creator and grader of the same product — not a matter of any individual evaluator's competence or honesty.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes what organizations like METR, the UK AI Safety Institute, and Apollo Research do?
options: They simply rerun the lab's own internal test suite and republish the same numbers
They each bring an independent lens — autonomy/agentic capability, government dangerous-capability testing, and deceptive/strategic behavior respectively — producing their own assessments
They only evaluate models after a lab has gone out of business
They exclusively provide marketing materials for frontier labs
questions.explain: Each organization has a distinct focus and conducts independent assessment rather than reproducing the lab's internal results.

questions.q: What characterizes a typical pre-deployment access agreement between a frontier lab and an external evaluator?
options: The evaluator has unlimited time and full model weight access with no restrictions
It is voluntary and lab-controlled: the lab decides who gets access, at what level, and for how long before a release date the lab sets
It is a legally mandated arrangement identical across every lab and jurisdiction
It gives the evaluator full control over whether the model is ever released
questions.explain: These agreements are a real improvement over pure self-regulation, but the lab retains control over access terms and timing.

questions.q: What is a common limitation external evaluators face even under a pre-deployment access agreement?
options: They typically lack model weights, limiting fine-tuning-based checks and deep interpretability analysis, and often have only days or weeks before launch
They have no limitations whatsoever compared to the lab's own internal team
They are legally forbidden from publishing any findings
They always have more time than the lab's own internal safety team
questions.explain: Weight access and compressed testing windows are real constraints that distinguish external evaluation from full, unconstrained adversarial access.

questions.q: What is the correct takeaway about a clean result from a third-party evaluation, according to this lesson?
options: It is a complete guarantee that the model has no dangerous capabilities whatsoever
It is meaningful and a real improvement over self-assessment, but not a complete guarantee given access and time constraints
It should be ignored entirely since external evaluators are never trustworthy
It means no further evaluation of the model is ever needed again
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns against treating an external eval's clean result as a complete guarantee, given the real access and time limits evaluators face.
